claims.text: Controlled post-deposition annealing in a low-oxygen atmosphere can form a lubricious oxide layer on a high-entropy-alloy surface.
The resulting oxide layer can reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate across a wide service-temperature range.
The initial material is an equimolar CuMoTaWV refractory high-entropy-alloy film produced by DC-magnetron sputtering.
The as-deposited CuMoTaWV film is nanocrystalline with an average grain size of about 18 nm.
The initial film was deposited without deliberate oxidation tailoring.
A post-deposition anneal at around 300 °C is applicable to the CuMoTaWV film system.
Performing the anneal under a low oxygen partial pressure will induce controlled surface oxidation.
The intervention should improve tribological performance at room temperature and around 300 °C.
Prior work tested the CuMoTaWV film tribologically at room temperature and 300 °C.
Controlled oxidation will produce a thin, homogeneous, finely dispersed sub-stoichiometric CuO or composition-adjusted mixed-oxide layer.
The proposed oxide layer will minimize direct metal-metal contact and act as a sacrificial lubricious film.
The oxide layer will reduce interfacial shear during sliding.
The nanograined structure promotes hardness through grain-boundary strengthening.
The combination of the oxide layer and nanograined structure will reduce friction and wear by suppressing severe adhesive and abrasive interactions.
Oxidation will reduce room-temperature coefficient of friction by about 30% relative to the untreated film.
Oxidation will mitigate the high coefficient of friction at elevated temperature.
Oxidation will reduce wear rate by roughly one order of magnitude across the tested temperature range.
The untreated film has a coefficient of friction of approximately 0.25 at room temperature and approximately 1.5 at 300 °C.
Overly aggressive oxidation may produce brittle, non-lubricious oxides that degrade tribological performance.
The lubricant layer may lose effectiveness above the thermal-stability range of the formed oxide.
